name: Louis Fettle, in Le Mai's house
head: fettle_louis

present_on_scene_date.note: His card says what is known of him in 1812.

associated_with.note: Currey's 'small cabin near the Kinzie house', read as one of the four houses of 1808 (pettell_cabin_1812); Le Mai's, since La Lime's was his own until June 1812.

not_in_this_household.note: His wife, an Indian woman (Quaife), is not named and not carded.

persons.name: Louis Fettle (Pettell)

age_band.note: Not recorded; settled here by 1803 with a wife, drawn at forty-five.

present_on_scene_date.note: In Kinzie's books down to 1812; only Quaife's guess ("Probably") puts him among the twelve militia of 15 August.

persons.note: A French-Canadian who was living at Chicago with an Indian wife when the garrison came in 1803, and whose name is in John Kinzie's books down to 1812; then he disappears. Quaife thinks him probably one of the twelve militia killed on 15 August. His home here is Le Mai's house: the hut Currey puts 'near the Kinzie house' is read as one of the four houses of 1808 under a later name (data/exclusions.json pettell_cabin_1812), La Lime's or Le Mai's, and La Lime lived in his until 17 June 1812 (L-1812-gathering-people-3500). His wife is not named or carded.

evidence.quote: he was a French-Canadian living here with an Indian wife when the garrison came in 1803
evidence.claim: French Canadian with an Indian wife, here in 1803

evidence.quote: His name occurs at intervals down to 1812, showing that he was a resident of Chicago during the entire period.
A man named Pettell also had a small cabin near the Kinzie house.
Probably Louis Fettle, who lived at Chicago from 1803 to 1812 and then disappeared from recorded history, was still another.
evidence.claim: Quaife's guess: one of the twelve militia
